I’m 34, a Pilates instructor, and I got divorced a couple of years ago. Lately, it feels like I’m on a seesaw. For about three months, I was flying high, full of energy. I'd bounce between feeling absolutely fantastic, like I could conquer anything, and then suddenly I’d snap at someone for the smallest thing. I was a whirlwind, picking up extra classes, redecorating my whole apartment at 2 AM, and honestly, sleep felt optional – I could go a few nights hardly sleeping and still feel totally fine. It never really caused big problems at work or anything, though.

But for the past year and a month, it’s been the complete opposite. I just feel… flat. I've been so slow, like my body is stuck in molasses; even walking feels like a chore. And my job, which I used to love, it just doesn't bring me joy anymore, even when I help a client reach a new goal. I'm drained all the time, everything takes so much effort, and it’s become really hard to even show up for my classes. It’s like I’m numb inside. This last episode has definitely messed things up for me, making it hard to feel motivated for anything. Though, it's never gotten so bad that I've needed to be hospitalized or felt like I was losing touch with reality.
D009-D008_h023.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h024.question:
Lately, I’ve been feeling so worn out, absolutely nothing brings me joy anymore, not even my usual crossword puzzles. My wife tries to talk to me, but it's like my brain just can’t catch up, and my responses are slow, if they come at all. And this exhaustion, it’s just constant, even after a full night’s sleep. This black cloud has been hanging over me for over a year now, making it hard to even get out of bed for my security guard shifts.

Before this, though, a few months ago, I had a stretch when I was practically buzzing with energy for about three months straight. I was snapping at everyone, getting aggressive over tiny things, and I’d be up all night, tackling projects around the house and feeling totally refreshed on just a couple hours of sleep. My wife would tell me to calm down, but I just felt great! But even then, I was still showing up for work and doing what I needed to do; it didn’t ever get so bad that I thought I needed to go to the hospital, and I certainly wasn’t hearing things or seeing things that weren't there. Looking back, it's quite a shift from how sluggish and down I am now.
D009-D008_h024.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder

D009-D008_h025.question:
"Lately, I just feel like I'm on a rollercoaster. For about three months, I was on top of the world, bouncing off the walls, needing to constantly be doing something. I'd be up at 4 AM, feeling totally refreshed after just a couple of hours of sleep, ready to tackle anything. My mood would swing from feeling incredible to snapping at my colleagues in a blink. It was exhausting for those around me, but I never felt like it completely derailed my life or my job, you know?

But that’s all gone now. For over a year, I've been in this deep slump. Getting out of bed feels like a monumental effort. My movements are slower, like I’m moving through treacle. I'm just so drained all the time, even after a full night's sleep. There's this constant, heavy sadness that just hangs over me. I’ve lost all motivation; even at work, which I used to love, it’s hard to find the energy to care. This part of it truly impacts my ability to function, unlike those high periods which, while intense, never got so out of hand that I needed to be hospitalized or anything like that. I definitely haven't had any delusions or hallucinations."

A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
